input.quote: PB shall notify SFJ in writing of the total amount of Development Costs (inclusive of all Development Costs paid or incurred since the Effective Date) that PB elects to have SFJ fund (the "Elected Total Amount"), which shall be no less than $110 million and no more than $120 million.
input.rationale:
This is a co-development funding agreement in which the payment flow runs toward us: SFJ funds up to $120m of Development Costs (§ 4.1, § 4.2), and our payments to SFJ under ARTICLE 6 are Approval Payments that only become due "following Regulatory Approval" (§ 6.1.1, § 6.1.2). There is no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall penalty or volume restriction imposed on PB, so the rule sits at the preferred position (fees only for what is actually delivered/contingent milestones).

We reviewed the two nearest analogues flagged in planning and neither functions as a take-or-pay on us: (i) the $110m floor on the Elected Total Amount (§ 4.2.3(ii)) is a floor on how much funding we must accept from SFJ, not on what we must buy, and it is only triggered after a Successful Phase 3 Interim Analysis; and (ii) the excess-cost allocation in § 4.1 / § 4.2.3 (Development Costs above $120m "will be borne by PB", plus the covenant to "spend at least an amount equal to the amount of funding paid by SFJ") is a use-of-proceeds and cost-overrun covenant on our own development programme rather than a purchase obligation to the counterparty. Both are further mitigated by our at-will exit in § 14.2.2, exercisable at any time after SFJ has paid or incurred $60m and before first Regulatory Approval, and by the Buy-Out Payment election in § 6.7. The 300% termination payment under § 14.2.2 is a priced financing return rather than a shortfall penalty and is addressed under the termination/exit-cost rules, not here. No redline proposed.
